To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) partial-order planning is a refinement search algorithm; (ii) different partial-order planning algorithms can be viewed as different instantiations of the refinement search algorithm; and (iii) the design choices in these instantiations trade one for the others in terms of their effects on search space size and planning cost.
(i) partial-order planners are refinement planners, and (ii) partial-order planners trade off the size of the search space and the cost of the refinements.

(1) refinement search is an effective framework for comparing the performance tradeoffs of various planning algorithms; (2) partial-order planning algorithms are specific instantiations thereof; (3) the different design choices of partial-order planning algorithms trade search space size and the cost of refining a partial order into a plan.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a better theoretical understanding of the design tradeoffs in partial-order planning and the empirical analysis of the performance consequences of these design choices.
understanding the design tradeoffs offered by refinement search and their effect on planning performance.
the development of a unifying framework for evaluating the performance tradeoffs in partial-order planning.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single best way of instantiating refinement search for partial-order planning.
refinement search provides an excellent framework for evaluating the performance tradeoffs in partial-order planning.

the performance of a planner is a function of its search space size, its refinement cost, and the cost of the problem instance, and that different planning algorithms can be viewed as instantiations of a single generalized algorithm that trade off these costs in different ways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
partial-order planning is not a single algorithm but a family of algorithms that differ in the design decisions made by the planner designer.

partial-order planning is not a monolithic algorithm but rather a family of algorithms that trade one design choice for another, and that the design choices are not independent but rather interact with each other in a complex manner.
refinement search is a powerful and expressive framework for analyzing the performance tradeoffs in partial-order planning.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a unified framework for comparing different planning algorithms allows us to understand the performance tradeoffs between these algorithms, and to design new algorithms that combine the desirable features of different algorithms.
the performance of a refinement planner depends on a complex interplay among many factors, and that there are no clear winners in this interplay.

, by using a common framework for expressing and comparing different planning algorithms, we can better understand the design tradeoffs offered by different planners and develop more effective planning algorithms.
